distractors.reason: We don't say 'listen quickly'. 'Quickly' describes speed of an action, not how well we pay attention.
'Loudly' describes volume. We don't use it to describe the quality of listening in 'listen loudly'.
'Slowly' describes speed. We don't say 'listen slowly' to mean paying attention.

l1_interference: Los hispanohablantes a veces colocan el adverbio antes del verbo, diciendo 'carefully listen' en vez del correcto 'listen carefully'. En inglés el adverbio va después del verbo.
explanation: In English, the adverb usually comes after the verb: listen carefully, speak fluently, work hard. Think of the adverb as describing how the action is done.

related_collocations.example: Please speak clearly so everyone can understand.
She works hard every day in class.

memory_tip: VERB + ADVERB = the adverb comes AFTER the verb: listen carefully, speak clearly, work hard
